title: Paul McCartney’s court hearing to dissolve The Beatles’ partnership – day nine | 1971
content:
3 March 1971 was the ninth day of Paul McCartney’s court hearing to have The Beatles’ business partnership dissolved.

Morris Finer, QC, the barrister for John Lennon, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr, continued arguing their case in London’s High Court on this day.

Finer defended the work of Allen Klein, The Beatles’ business manager, saying that the appointment of an official receiver to manage the band’s income would result in the end of their business operations.

The case had been presented as making out that Mr McCartney had been cheated. The truth was that it was a question of whether the commission payable to Mr Klein was ‘of right’…

The whole object of this operation is to poison the court against Mr Klein and say that he is dangerous and it is for the benefit of
everybody to get him out.

Morris Finer, QC

The judge, Mr Justice Stamp, was evidently growing impatient with the length of the case. After Finer suggested a break in proceedings on the following day, he refused the request, telling Finer: “This was going to be a five-day case, and then a six-day case. Where are we now? It is the ninth day. It seems to be going on since time immemorial.”
